cards.title: Choose FBA or FBM before setting up a seller account
cards.summary: FBA hands pick/pack/ship to Amazon for per-order fees; FBM means you ship yourself, and the source's preference is FBA for a semi-passive operation.
cards.use_when: Deciding your fulfilment model before registering an Amazon seller account or sourcing inventory.
steps: Understand the two models: FBA (Fulfilment by Amazon) means you send stock to Amazon's warehouse and they pick, pack and ship each order, charging fulfilment fees that reduce your margin. FBM (Fulfilment by Merchant) means you ship every order yourself.

Source view: the presenter chooses FBA because he wants a lifestyle, semi-passive business rather than packing orders at home. Treat this as his personal preference, not a universal rule — FBM can suit heavy, fragile, low-volume or made-to-order items.
Note that your choice changes the fee lines in every profitability calculation, so fix the model before you analyse products.
If in doubt, run one small FBA test batch and compare actual per-unit fulfilment fees against your own shipping cost before committing your full range.
Verify current fee schedules and programme terms in Seller Central, as Amazon changes them.
caveats: Source is a single practitioner's preference, not a benchmark; FBM is not inherently worse.
cards.source_name: Beginners Guide To Amazon FBA In 2025 (1).docx

cards.title: Pick an Amazon business model: arbitrage, wholesale or private label
cards.summary: The three Amazon selling routes differ in capital, competition and learning curve; the source suggests starting with arbitrage/wholesale before private label.
cards.use_when: Choosing which Amazon selling model to launch next quarter and how much capital to allocate.
steps: Map the three routes as the source describes them: (1) Retail/online arbitrage — buy discounted stock from supermarkets or retail websites and resell on Amazon; lowest capital, quick-cash but not scalable and often capped (e.g. quantity limits per order). (2) Wholesale — buy branded products in bulk from a wholesaler or the brand and resell at retail price; more scalable, no need to create demand or run ads, source cites roughly £1,000 starting capital. (3) Private label — create your own brand, source from China, build your own listing and run ads; source cites roughly £5,000–£10,000 needed for stock, ads, images, listing, barcodes and trademark.
Note the trade-off the source highlights: wholesale means other sellers can buy the same branded product and compete on your listing; private label removes that but raises cost and learning curve.
His recommendation for beginners is to start with wholesale or arbitrage to learn how Amazon works, then move to private label — cite this as his opinion, not a rule.
Choose your route now because it determines which product-analysis checks (BSR, seller count, ROI) are even relevant.
caveats: Arbitrage and wholesale-specific sourcing metrics (BSR, seller counts, 30% ROI) do not transfer to private label or your own DTC store.
Capital figures are the presenter's stated examples, not guarantees.
cards.source_name: Beginners Guide To Amazon FBA In 2025 (1).docx

cards.title: Register a UK Amazon Professional seller account and pass verification
cards.summary: Practical setup sequence for a UK seller account, including the live video verification call and proof documents you must have ready.
cards.use_when: Opening a new Amazon seller account in the UK and preparing for identity verification.
steps: Go to the Amazon seller sign-up page for your marketplace (e.g. sell on Amazon UK) and register either with an existing shopping account or a new one.

Compare current UK Individual and Professional charges and needed features. Do not mistake a volume-based cost recommendation for a hard unit limit; use current local prices rather than assuming US fees apply.
Register the account under the name of someone who holds both a valid proof of ID and a proof of address, because verification checks both.
Expect a live verification video call with an Amazon employee where you hold your ID next to your face, and be ready to upload your proof-of-address document.
After submitting, verification commonly completes within 72 hours (the source has seen it take as little as 1–2 hours), then add your bank/charge and payment details in Seller Central.
If the account is rejected, suspended or deactivated, you can appeal directly or engage a specialist to prepare a detailed appeal.
Reasons cited for rejection include details not matching your ID documents, a previously suspended account, or missing information Amazon requested.
caveats: Specific fees and timelines are UK- and date-specific; verify the current sign-up interface and fees in Seller Central.
cards.source_name: Beginners Guide To Amazon FBA In 2025 (1).docx

cards.title: Set up a seller account you can actually trade from
cards.summary: The account needs verified identity, a linked bank account and the correct plan before any listing work begins.
cards.use_when: Preparing a newly approved seller account before adding your first ASIN.
steps: Before you can sell, complete the tasks the dashboard flags, including adding the bank account Amazon will use to pay you and to charge fees.
Do not begin sourcing or shipping until verification has passed and payment details are registered, otherwise you cannot receive funds.
Keep your proof of ID and proof of address consistent with the name on the account so future reviews or reinstatements are simpler.
Set your account to the correct marketplace and only enable the marketplaces you actually intend to sell in when creating listings, so you do not accidentally expose stock abroad.
Treat the account as the asset: the source notes suspensions are a real risk, and appeals are harder once a prior suspension exists.
caveats: The exact dashboard tasks and screens change; follow the current on-screen guidance.

cards.title: Analyse a resale ASIN with four pass/fail checks
cards.summary: Screen any wholesale or arbitrage product against BSR, seller count, Amazon-as-competitor and ROI before buying.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to buy a specific branded ASIN for Amazon wholesale or arbitrage.
steps: Check Best Seller Rank, found under the listing's 'see all information' or product-details area. The source's rule of thumb is BSR under 100,000, because the lower the rank the faster the product sells — treat 100,000 as his guideline, not a fixed law.
Check actual selling eligibility, authentic supply documentation and whether the product exactly matches the ASIN. Competitor seller count is not proof of permission to sell.

Check Amazon is not on the listing. Open the buy box and check 'sold by' — if it says Amazon, avoid it, because Amazon typically undercuts and wins the buy box (cited case: Amazon priced more than £10 below the next cheapest seller). 'Amazon Warehouse' is acceptable because it is used stock.

Check ROI of at least 30%. Use Amazon's revenue calculator with the ASIN, set your sell price (source suggests matching the lowest FBA seller), enter cost of goods, and compute ROI = profit ÷ cost of goods × 100.
Only sell if all four checks pass. The source allows one adjustment: for a fast-selling item he would accept around 20% ROI.
caveats: BSR and 30% ROI are this presenter's arbitrage/wholesale heuristics, not universal standards, and are not appropriate for private label or DTC.
Check gating/eligibility and current fee structures before buying.
cards.source_name: Beginners Guide To Amazon FBA In 2025 (1).docx

cards.title: Calculate Amazon contribution, inventory ROI and applicable fee taxes
cards.summary: Include the complete per-unit cost stack and the seller's actual tax treatment when screening inventory.
cards.use_when: Judging whether a UK ASIN clears your profit threshold before committing to buy stock.
steps: Use the marketplace revenue calculator with the actual ASIN or dimensions, price, weight and fulfillment method.
Include landed product cost, selling and fulfillment fees, prep, labels, inbound charges, storage, expected returns and advertising where relevant.
Check fee invoices and the business's tax treatment; include non-recoverable tax costs and do not automatically add a blanket VAT percentage to every estimate.
Inventory ROI = contribution per unit / inventory cost per unit x 100; define the cost base consistently. £5.40 / £25 = 21.6%.
Compare contribution, inventory turnover and cash exposure together; the source's 20-30% thresholds are heuristics, not universal profit requirements.
caveats: Contribution is not final net profit after all overhead.
Use the relevant marketplace and verified tax inputs; calculator estimates may omit some costs.
cards.source_name: Beginners Guide To Amazon FBA In 2025 (1).docx

cards.title: Run a 10–50 unit test order before committing to wholesale stock
cards.summary: The first order for any new wholesale product should be small so you can validate sell-through, competition and eligibility before scaling.
cards.use_when: Placing your first purchase order for a newly validated wholesale ASIN.
steps: Buy a test shipment of roughly 10 to 50 units rather than a full pallet on your first order, as the source recommends.

Use the test to check three things: whether the product actually sells at your price, whether other sellers jump on and undercut you, and whether the product has any restrictions or problems (e.g. gating) that leave you holding stock.
Compare the test result against your original product checks (BSR, seller count, ROI) before reordering in volume.
Only scale the order once the test shows the margin holding at real selling prices after Amazon fees and VAT.
Model the downside explicitly: the source's warning is that if you order 400 units and the product is restricted or undercut, your cash is trapped in unsellable inventory.
caveats: Test size is described as a range for beginners; some gated categories may require 10–100 units plus a supplier invoice to become eligible.
cards.source_name: Beginners Guide To Amazon FBA In 2025 (1).docx

cards.title: Add an existing ASIN to your inventory instead of creating a listing
cards.summary: Match existing listings by ASIN, sell at the lowest FBA price and select Amazon's barcode to avoid commingled stock.
cards.use_when: Listing a validated wholesale or arbitrage product you are ready to sell on Amazon.
steps: In Seller Central go to Catalog > Add Product, paste the product's ASIN (found under 'see all information') and search rather than building a brand-new listing.

If the result says condition new 'apply to sell' you are gated. To get ungated the source's method is to buy 10 units — sometimes 100 — of the exact product from a wholesale supplier and upload an invoice matching your Amazon account or company name.
Once eligible, set condition as New and click 'Sell this product'; you are joining the existing listing, not creating one.
Price to match or sit close to the lowest FBA seller on the listing. Filter the other-sellers view by Prime to isolate FBA sellers.
Set fulfilment channel to Amazon (FBA) and disable any other marketplaces you do not want to sell in, then save and finish.

At the barcode field choose 'Amazon's barcode only' even if the product already has a manufacturer barcode, so Amazon can attribute commingled shipments to you rather than confusing your stock with another seller's on the same ASIN.
Allow around 15 minutes for the offer to appear in your inventory.
caveats: Gating thresholds and invoice requirements vary by category and brand; verify with Seller Central.
Sticking your own Amazon barcode over the manufacturer barcode is the source's commingling safeguard — this alters the physical unit, so confirm it does not conflict with the brand's requirements.
cards.source_name: Beginners Guide To Amazon FBA In 2025 (1).docx

cards.title: Create an FBA shipping plan and respect box size and weight limits
cards.summary: Create an inbound plan from actual units, packaging and current marketplace requirements.
cards.use_when: Building a shipment plan to send stock from your premises into an Amazon fulfilment centre.
steps: Start the current Send to Amazon or replenishment workflow with the correct origin and inventory.
Check category-specific prep, expiration, barcode and labeling requirements; fragility alone does not determine prep needs.
Confirm who will prepare and label each unit before dispatch; do not assume Amazon offers the services shown in an older tutorial.
Enter accurate unit counts, box contents, dimensions and weights; check current limits and exceptions for the receiving marketplace.
Choose an eligible parcel or pallet route and compare actual carrier charges.
Check charges and cancellation terms before confirming; do not assume a universal 24-hour free cancellation window.
caveats: Source UK dimensions, label fees and carrier recommendations are historical examples, not current global requirements.
cards.source_name: Beginners Guide To Amazon FBA In 2025 (1).docx

cards.title: Print SKU and box labels and schedule a UPS collection
cards.summary: After confirming the shipment you still must print labels, get the tracking ID and book a UPS pickup — receiving tracking alone is not the end of the process.
cards.use_when: Finalising an FBA shipment after confirming charges in Seller Central.
steps: Print SKU/unit labels, choosing standard or thermal format for your printer. On a normal A4 printer the source uses A4 label sheets so the labels print and peel off.
Print box labels and carrier labels on A4 label sheets (he cites 1 x 139mm or equivalent templates) — you will get a UPS label and an Amazon box label.
Do not stop when tracking details appear. Copy the tracking ID from 'view tracking details'.
Go to UPS's schedule-a-pickup page, confirm you have a prepaid UPS shipping label, and paste the tracking ID; separate multiple tracking IDs with commas.
Enter your address, the number of packages/boxes, and the total weight, then flag whether the shipment exceeds 32kg.
Choose the collection date and a 4-hour window (the source notes UPS offers something like 11:00–15:00 or 12:00–17:00 and you cannot shrink the window); alternatively drop off at a collection point.
Review and confirm the booking; from collection onwards Amazon handles picking, packing and shipping to customers.
caveats: Carrier interfaces, offered time windows and templates change — verify the current UPS booking flow.
The drop-off vs collection choice affects cost and control; the source simply prefers collection for convenience.
